market_brief: Friday turned the AI unwind into a full-blown rout: the S&P 500 closed about -3.7% and the Dow about -1.9%, both now in correction, while the Nasdaq Composite fell about -5.3% to erase its 2026 gain (the 20:18 UTC snapshot already showed SOX -10.2%, NDX -5.0% and VIX 34.4). Nvidia sank ~14% on a reported SEC accounting review, with AMD, Micron and Broadcom down 12-14% and Anthropic off ~8.5% to ~$89, still above its $83 IPO price. Haven bids drove the 10Y down ~14bp to ~4.91% even though a December Fed hike stays ~97% priced and Governor Cook warned of falling 'behind the curve'; DXY was flat near 103.8. Deleveraging hit everything liquid: gold -4.6% to ~$3,515, silver -8%, bitcoin -5.7% to ~$58.4k (lowest since July) and ether -8.5%, while Brent slipped 2.6% to ~$89.6. India stayed the outlier: Sensex +1.1% to 83,920 and Nifty +1.1% to 25,800.6 with Nifty Bank at a record, on heavy FPI inflows and a firmer rupee (~92.7).
ai_brief: Markets dominated AI news: Nvidia's seventh straight losing week, a reported SEC review and California's subpoena, plus Anthropic's greenshoe lifting its record IPO to a reported ~$93.5B. On the product side, Thinking Machines shipped open-weights Inkling 2 Mini, Tencent released Hy4 Flash weights and Google gave Gemini computer control on Macs. Math claims drew the most discussion: Anthropic touted Claude Fable 5.2 physics and Lean results, and an Anthropic mathematician claimed a Generalized Riemann Hypothesis proof that awaits outside review. Policy turned sharper, with Trump floating a tax on US firms building data centers abroad and Cursor weighing dropping Chinese open models.

items.headline: S&P 500 and Dow close in correction; Nasdaq drops ~5.3% to erase its 2026 gain
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell about 3.7% to ~6,910 and the Dow about 1.9% to ~48,147, both now more than 10% below their record closes, while the Nasdaq Composite lost about 5.3% to ~22,618. Yorkville's Dan Ives listed seven catalysts, including Jensen Huang's exit, China regulatory fears, liquidity drained by the Anthropic IPO and hawkish Fed talk.

items.headline: Nvidia plunges ~14% on reported SEC accounting review; AMD, Micron, Broadcom fall 12-14%
items.summary: Citing Reuters, TradingKey said SEC enforcement staff are looking at possible accounting issues at Nvidia; the SEC declined to comment. Nvidia closed near $126, AMD and Micron fell ~13-14%, and Broadcom ~12%, dragging Intel, ASML and Applied Materials lower.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic closes ~8.5% lower near $89 on day two; greenshoe lifts IPO to a reported ~$93.5B
items.summary: Anthropic ended its second session around $88.6-88.9, down from its $111.50 opening trade but still above the $83 offer, per market recaps. Underwriters reportedly exercised the overallotment, adding about $12.2B and taking total proceeds to a record ~$93.5B.

items.headline: Fed's Cook says waiting to hike risks getting 'behind the curve'; December hike ~97% priced
items.summary: Speaking in Santiago, Governor Lisa Cook argued for raising rates now, having dissented in October against a hold. CME FedWatch showed roughly 97.5% odds of a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC despite the equity rout.

items.headline: Update: 10-year yield falls ~13bp to ~4.92% as haven buying deepens
items.summary: Treasuries rallied through the US session, with the 5-year near 4.70% and the 30-year near 5.31%, and long-duration TLT up ~1.4%. The move came despite hawkish Fed pricing, pointing to flight-to-quality demand.

items.headline: Background: SEC civil probe and California AG pressure follow Huang's resignation
items.summary: InvestmentNews summarised the WSJ report of an SEC civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors, alongside California AG Rob Bonta's concerns over chip diversion to China. Treasury Secretary Bessent reportedly wants answers from Nvidia's board within ten days; interim CEO Colette Kress raised FY2028 growth guidance to ~75%.

items.headline: Sensex jumps 898 points to 83,920; Nifty 25,800.6 and Nifty Bank at a record
items.summary: India rallied ~1.1% while Asia sank, led by Apollo Hospitals (+5.3%), Axis Bank (+4.7%) and Max Healthcare; Titan and Tata Steel lagged. FIIs bought a net ₹7,411 crore on Thursday and FPIs put in ~₹30,668 crore over the week, though India VIX rose 7.5% to 17.3.

items.headline: Flows: 'sell global AI, buy India' rotation brings record ~$12.2B of November FPI inflows
items.summary: HDFC Sky described investors dumping AI-linked global stocks for Indian equities, with November FPI inflows at a record ~$12.21B. The rupee gained 62 paise to ~92.67/USD, a seven-month high, though BSE breadth was negative.

items.headline: Gap jumps ~11-12% on a narrow beat; Intuit closes ~13% lower on a weak fiscal 2027 outlook
items.summary: Gap had its best day of the year despite trimming full-year guidance, with its CEO calling the consumer 'resilient but discerning'. Intuit's fiscal 2027 EPS guide of $22.88-23.12 fell well short of ~$27.30 consensus, and the stock closed down ~12.8%.

items.headline: CrowdStrike reportedly in talks to acquire Zscaler; Zscaler up ~18% after hours
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that CrowdStrike is in talks to buy Zscaler, which would create a combined company worth about $267B. Neither company has confirmed a deal.

items.headline: Biotech setbacks: Savara -18% and Belite Bio -16% on FDA timing delays
items.summary: Savara fell after the FDA said it would not act by the Nov 22 target date, and Belite Bio slid after its review was extended to May 2027. WeRide fell ~8.6% amid the broad tech sell-off.

items.headline: Update: Europe closes sharply lower; STOXX 600 -2%, Euro Stoxx 50 -2.8%, DAX -2.6%
items.summary: European indices extended losses into the close as the US sell-off deepened, capping the STOXX 600's worst week since March (about -5.8% per the closing data). Chip and tech names led the declines, while the FTSE 100 held up better at about -1%.

items.headline: Update: gold settles ~4.5% lower near $3,515; silver down ~8%
items.summary: Metals were sold again to meet margin and cover equity losses, with gold ending near $3,515-3,519 and silver around $40.75, a weekly loss of roughly 17% for silver. Platinum and copper also fell 3-5%.

items.headline: Brent slips ~2.6% to ~$89.6, down ~23% in November on US-Iran de-escalation hopes
items.summary: Crude extended its weekly decline as risk assets slid; HDFC Sky noted Brent is down about 23% this month on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation, a tailwind for India's import bill and rupee.

items.headline: Update: bitcoin breaks below $59,000 to its lowest since July; on pace for worst month since June 2022
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 5-6% to ~$58.3k, leaving it down about 23% in November, and ether lost ~8.5% to near $1,600. Crypto has traded as a high-beta extension of the AI sell-off.

items.headline: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on US companies building AI data centers abroad
items.summary: In White House remarks, Trump reportedly singled out a planned Finland project but gave no rate or timeline. The threat adds policy risk for hyperscalers' overseas capex plans.

items.headline: Thanksgiving week: Tokyo shut Monday, US PCE and holiday-shortened trading; RBI and Fed in early December
items.summary: Tokyo is closed Monday; Analog Devices and Medtronic (Nov 24), Deere (Nov 25) and US PCE inflation are due before US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and shorten Friday. Further out: RBI MPC Dec 2-4, FOMC Dec 8-9 and BoJ Dec 17-18.

items.headline: Nvidia's seventh straight losing week is its longest since 2008
items.summary: After Friday's ~14% drop, Nvidia has reportedly lost about $2.6T of market value since Oct 6, a slide that followed Jensen Huang's resignation and the reported SEC accounting review.

items.headline: California AG opens investigation and subpoenas Nvidia over China chip and disclosure concerns
items.summary: The probe reportedly covers whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether Nvidia misled investors. It adds to the federal scrutiny following Huang's exit.

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.2 solved two black-hole physics problems and verified Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean
items.summary: Anthropic describes the results as peer-review ready; they have not yet been independently reviewed.

items.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims a Claude-assisted Generalized Riemann Hypothesis proof; a rival claim draws pushback
items.summary: Levent Alpöge posted a four-page note with Lean code, which has no outside confirmation yet. A separate same-day GRH claim by Alessandro Masullo was described by Stanford's Ravi Vakil as 'all human, no AI'.

items.headline: Thinking Machines releases open-weights Inkling 2 Mini, a 26B MoE that runs on a 32GB laptop
items.summary: The model has 26.4B parameters with 3.4B active per token, and the company reports 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1.

items.headline: Tencent releases Hy4 Flash weights for local deployment
items.summary: The open-weights text-and-image model supports up to 1M tokens of context, adding to a steady run of Chinese open releases.

items.headline: Gemini gains computer use on Mac for paid US subscribers
items.summary: Gemini can now organise local files, fill in forms and operate Mac apps, initially in English for US AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers.

items.headline: OpenAI introduces MedChemBench; GPT-6.2 Astra scores 84.5%
items.summary: The new benchmark has 99 medicinal-chemistry problems; OpenAI reports its top reasoning setting scored 84.5%.

items.headline: Cursor tells House committees it may phase out Chinese open-weight models
items.summary: The coding-tool maker cited geopolitical risk, notable because its Composer 2 model is reportedly built on Moonshot's Kimi K2.5.

items.headline: Cognition reportedly fields offers near $75B; LangChain raises $300M at $3B
items.summary: Cognition (Devin) is reportedly in early talks to raise $2B+ at a $70-80B valuation, weeks after a $48B round. LangChain's Series C was reportedly led by CapitalG with GIC and IVP.

items.headline: Meta's Muse agent reportedly mixed up conversations and exposed private data to testers
items.summary: Employees testing the assistant reportedly saw other users' messages and bank balances; Meta said staff test builds with unreleased features.

items.headline: AI-assisted cyberattack disrupts European Commission payroll and reimbursement systems
items.summary: Officials were reportedly checking whether personal data was compromised after systems were temporarily affected.

items.headline: Newsletter focus: the GRH proof claims, Anthropic's IPO, and whether the AI bubble just burst
items.summary: AI Weekly led with the dueling Riemann claims and named Nvidia the most-covered company of the week, while The Neuron and others led on Anthropic's debut and agent privacy lapses.
